expected_level_description: You can: - give independent legal advice in your areas of practice - explain legal risk in plain English and recommend practical options - advise on decisions with legal effect, such as contract awards, data sharing, and changes to services - decide when to instruct external lawyers or counsel

You can: - draft and negotiate complex agreements, such as software licences, cloud hosting, system integration, and data processing agreements - advise on risk allocation, including liability caps, service levels, exit, and escrow - make sure contracts protect patient data, service continuity, and the organisation's rights in its software and data - write and maintain contract templates and playbooks

You can: - research complex or novel questions, such as how existing law applies to new technology - analyse conflicting sources and reach a reasoned view - track changes in law and guidance and explain their effect on the organisation

You can: - advise on data protection, the duty of confidentiality, and information access law for digital services - draft and negotiate data sharing agreements and data processing terms, including international transfers - advise on data protection impact assessments for new technology, such as AI and analytics platforms - advise on data breaches, regulator enquiries, and complaints
You can: - check tender documents for consistency and completeness - support the record keeping needed to show a fair and transparent process

You can: - collect and organise documents and evidence for a case - prepare chronologies, bundles, and witness statement drafts - liaise with external lawyers, insurers, or indemnity schemes on routine matters
You can: - check intellectual property clauses in routine agreements - keep records of licences and registered rights - explain the main open source licence types and their conditions

You can: - identify important stakeholders and communicate with them clearly and regularly - tailor communication to stakeholders' needs and work with them to build relationships while meeting user needs - build and reach consensus with stakeholders - work to improve stakeholder relationships using evidence to explain decisions

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
